findings.claim: Candidate accountability gap: the analyze handoff verdict tally accounts for 10 decided candidates (4 adopt, 1 adopt-provisional, 2 build, 1 adopt-values-only, 1 reject, 1 defer), but the artifact evaluates exactly 7. Three candidates (2 adopt + 1 adopt-provisional per the tally) are absent with no decision_rationale, so the adopt decisions the spec stage must consume cannot be verified from this packet.
findings.evidence: Artifact ends at analysis.md line 537 immediately after build_required; candidates present: citation-merge (build), onyx-budgets (adopt-values-only), onyx-parallel-cap (adopt-and-improve), uar-native-runner (reject), workspace-split (defer), deep-research-bench (adopt), multipass-report (build) = 7 total. Handoff tally sums to 10. The artifact never states that candidates were merged or dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: Include all 10 evaluated candidates in analysis.md (or embed library-candidates.json, listed as an analyze output, in the review packet) with an explicit decision_rationale for each of the 3 unaccounted adopt/adopt-provisional candidates, or state the consolidation that reduced 10 to 7.
findings.what_would_change_this: library-candidates.json (declared as an analyze-stage output but not embedded in the packet) containing the 3 remaining evaluated candidates with rationales, or an in-artifact consolidation note mapping 10 tallied decisions onto the 7 presented candidates.
disconfirming: The handoff tally may describe a pre-consolidation candidate list later merged (e.g., adopt-and-improve folding several adopt candidates into one), in which case the gap is documentation-only rather than missing evaluation.

findings.claim: Producer attribution is inconsistent across the packet: packet producer_model is 'unknown', the artifact's embedded prior-review metadata names producer 'claude-opus-5', and the review invocation asserts kimi-for-coding/k3. Cross-model verification claims (judge k3 vs producer) are unauditable as packaged.
findings.evidence: packet.json producer_model = 'unknown'; artifact 'Unresolved review findings' section records judge k3 with producer claude-opus-5 across two PASS rounds; invocation instruction sets producer_model kimi-for-coding/k3 for this findings file.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a single authoritative producer_model in packet.json and reconcile it with the embedded review metadata, or annotate the embedded metadata as referring to an earlier draft.
findings.what_would_change_this: A packet or stage receipt showing the final artifact was regenerated by k3 after the claude-opus-5 draft, with the embedded metadata explicitly marked as historical.
disconfirming: The embedded metadata may legitimately refer to an earlier draft producer while k3 produced the final artifact; the 'unknown' packet value may be a templating gap rather than a provenance defect.

findings.claim: Handoff chronology contradicts pipeline order: assess.handoff.json reports completion 2026-09-10/2026-09-11T23:02:56Z, while the analyze handoff and the artifact are dated 2026-09-08 (completedAt 2026-09-08T13:14:02Z). Analyze appears to predate completion of its predecessor stage, undermining provenance of the artifact's stated inputs (assessment.md).
findings.evidence: prior_handoffs: assess.handoff.json completedAt 2026-09-11T23:02:56Z (completed 2026-09-10, nextStage analyze); analyze handoff completedAt 2026-09-08T13:14:02Z; artifact header dated 2026-09-08 and claims assessment.md (5/5 NOT MET, V1-V4 resolved) as input.
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile or annotate the timestamps (e.g., note an assess re-run after analyze, or normalize timezone/clock source) so stage ordering is auditable.
findings.what_would_change_this: A stage log showing assess was re-executed after analyze for an unrelated reason, or evidence the two timestamps come from different clock sources.
disconfirming: assess may have been re-run after analyze completed, making the later assess timestamp irrelevant to the analyze artifact's provenance.
Timestamps may originate from different machines or timezone conventions.

findings.claim: Adoption-relevant landscape facts are asserted without retrieval provenance: onyx '31975 stars pushed 2026-09-08', deep_research_bench '827 stars pushed 2026-05-11', licences NOASSERTION and Apache-2.0. The spec stage cannot distinguish fetched facts from model memory, and star counts decay in evidentiary value within days.
findings.evidence: artifact library-candidates entries for onyx-budgets and deep-research-bench carry star counts, push dates, licence strings, and pinned_commit 469cce54ea7f6a63c163d3d9fec879cf289ec484 with no retrieval tool or UTC access date recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: Attach retrieval source and UTC access date (e.g., 'gh api repos/<owner>/<repo> at <timestamp>') to each external-repository claim, matching the diligence already applied to the pinned commit.
findings.what_would_change_this: An analyze-stage retrieval receipt (outside the packet) logging live fetches for these statistics on the analysis date.
disconfirming: The same-day push date for onyx (2026-09-08, equal to the analysis date) suggests a live fetch did occur and only the citation of it is missing.

findings.claim: The analyze handoff's blocking warnings are not explicitly dispositioned in the artifact: D-A (launchd PATH fix as fallback strategy B blocker) and D-B (C-01 generated-artifact desync requiring byte-identical regeneration proof) appear nowhere in build_required or the open-questions section, risking silent loss before spec.
findings.evidence: analyze handoff warnings (1)-(3) name D-03a, D-A, D-B and the NOASSERTION caution; artifact build_required items (1)-(7) and section 5 open questions (D-03a, V4, UAR-REM-002, q4) reference D-03a and NOASSERTION but never D-A or D-B.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line disposition per handoff warning (addressed-by <build_required item>, deferred-to spec, or rejected-because <reason>) so the spec stage does not need to re-derive coverage.
findings.what_would_change_this: Evidence that D-A and D-B are owned by a stage other than analyze/spec by design, or that build_required item (6) budgets/force-complete is intended to subsume them.
disconfirming: D-A and D-B may be deliberately scoped to the spec or execute stages rather than analyze.
build_required item (6) may be intended to cover D-B's regeneration-proof requirement implicitly.
